observed_risk.precise_scope: The pre-change wrapper default report branch was already read-only. The reviewed bridge clear_instruction_flow_override endpoint is a mutator, not a safe dry-run/property query. Do not misreport a default wrapper mutation that was not observed.
observed_risk.unsafe_apply: The former --apply path used that mutator, then legacy disassemble_bytes with a null restricted AddressSet and a boolean wired to Ghidra followFlow. It lacked exact FlowOverride/fallthrough/body metadata preimages, an atomic rollback transaction and an existing-function-body update; it could save after warning that the body tail remained incomplete.
observed_risk.read_limit: No current typed read route implemented here supplies the exact flow, fallthrough and no-return properties. The prior explicitly read-only inline query was rejected by the existing disabled-script gate. No new property query, guessed endpoint, script workaround or server change is introduced.

old_control_flow: Parse --apply/--record/tail options; read config, instantiate and verify Ghidra Client, read disk PE and existing JSON repair record.
Read disassemble_function, compute/print gaps. Without --apply, return after advertising --apply as the way to clear overrides and decode gaps; no default write occurred.

With --apply, acquire coordination lock/check leases, then post clear_instruction_flow_override and disassemble_bytes for each eligible gap; explicit-tail mode clears all matching free-call overrides again.
Re-decompile/report remaining gaps, write repair records and save_program even when the separate stored-body extension remains incomplete.
new_control_flow: Immediately reject any --apply argument with concrete missing bounded/atomic-route and exact-preimage requirements, before config/record access, Client creation, PE reads or any Ghidra request.
For default/--dry-run reporting, preserve function/tail parsing, verified Client reads and existing gap computation. --record remains accepted but the record file is neither read nor modified.

Only Client.verify GETs list_project_files/get_current_program_info and listing GET disassemble_function are reachable through the real read client. Report a conditional plan and state that exact flags, cause and body completion were not established.

The former POST helper, URL write imports, mutation endpoint calls, lock/mutation branch, record writes and save retry path are removed. No guessed capability detection or hidden bypass flag replaces them.
unsupported_apply_message: Unsupported --apply: an attested bounded/atomic callable repair route and exact flow/fallthrough, body and metadata preimages are required. The legacy flow-clearing/disassembly/save path is disabled. No Ghidra requests or mutations were made. Run without --apply for a conditional read-only report.
compatibility: Existing default report invocation and bsp.py ghidra flow remain read-only; explicit --dry-run is documented and follows the same report path.

Multiple functions, explicit tail bounds and --tail-rethrow argument requirements are preserved. load_pe, listing, find_gaps and tail_terminator helper source is unchanged after newline normalization.

--record <path> remains accepted for report invocations and leaves existing bytes unchanged. It no longer parses an unused JSON record, so malformed prior records do not block a read-only report; a missing path now produces a clear error.

All --apply invocations intentionally exit before connecting. This holds the unsafe legacy repair workflow rather than claiming a safe replacement exists. Previously retained repair records are not migrated, deleted or relabeled.
The report no longer attributes every gap to confirmed CALL_RETURN or recommends --apply. Tail reporting remains a boundary hint, not whole-Native validation or Ghidra body admission.
required_future_route: Independent review and attestation of a concrete callable bounded/atomic route; a descriptive endpoint name, dry-run flag, or script enable setting is not that attestation.

Direct exact preimages: local flow override, separate fallthrough flag/default/effective targets, callee no-return/thunk chain, Function ID/body ranges, all metadata/comments/references, full-byte ownership and unchanged original/live byte evidence.
Exclusive leases and coordination lock, existing saved-project checkpoint, proper analysis worker suppression, one owned transaction with rollback on any failed assertion.

Explicit restricted AddressSet disassembly with followFlow=false, preservation of existing code, validation of the recomputed candidate body before setting the same existing Function, with no deletion/recreation or overlapping owner edits.

Full postconditions for bytes, instruction starts, body, flow, metadata, references and neighbors, followed by saved-project receipt, refreshed exports and persistence readback; rollback must not undo unrelated work.
See docs/CC12_WORLD_DESTRUCTOR_LISTING_REPAIR_DESIGN.md for the concrete 00904C40 design. This tooling change supplies none of its missing live preimages or repair execution.
